baseline.observed: Original latest fetch or JSON-body stall leaves loading/aria-busy; no scheduled timeout/abort signal exists. Explicit successful retry recovers. The baseline 30sec scheduler horizon was simulated.

acceptanceResults: One 10000ms deadline spans fetch and JSON parsing and independently settles UI failure even when a synthetic reader ignores native abort. Timeout exposes retry state without stale order actions or an automatic retry.
Fresh invocation retires the prior request/timer. Latest ownership and per-request finally prevent retired completion, timer or cleanup from erasing current state or cancelling a newer read.

Monotonic expiry is checked before JSON parsing and after full read; retired late headers do not start body parsing. Focused boundary tests and removed-guard mutants verify late completions cannot win delayed timer scheduling.
Previous response-order/filter/copy/support browser checks remain valid; explicit retry restores selected-filter evidence and usable support.
Genuine HTTP fetch stall at private loopback raises native AbortError and closes the server response without server end.

Genuine native Response.json consumes an unfinished HTTP JSON stream: headers release after simulated6000ms, then another4001ms triggers the original total deadline, native body AbortError and server close. Explicit retry succeeds.
A native superseded HTTP read is aborted, its server response closes, and advancing its old deadline cannot remove new success. Final live cancel handle is null.
Reviewed 320px timeout and recovery images show readable failure/retry wording, no stale action rows during failure, persistent general support and restored completed evidence after retry.

limitations: Controlled clocks do not prove ten seconds of real network wall time or timing under suspended/throttled browser execution; late results are rejected when sampled monotonic time expires.

Native streaming-body cancellation is verified in isolated Chrome HTTP loopback only; real provider/TLS/network conditions, Telegram/iOS/WebKit, human comprehension and screen-reader announcements remain unverified.

Synthetic noncooperative promises may continue internally after UI retirement, but cannot publish stale UI. No new backend writer, retry loop, wallet/signature authority or money action is introduced.
Next receipt/evidence inconsistency is a valid-response content issue; past-tense receipt submission can remain historically true. No real customer incidence or misunderstanding was measured.
